definitions.explanation: Doing something without thinking; an action done despite not intending to.

examples.japanese: つい{笑|わら}ってしまった。
つい{食|た}べ{過|す}ぎてしまった。
つい{本音|ほんね}を{言|い}ってしまった。
examples.english: I inadvertently spoke my true feelings.

examples.japanese: {仕事中|しごとちゅう}についスマホを{見|み}てしまうことがある。
examples.english: I sometimes find myself looking at my phone during work.

examples.japanese: やめようと{思|おも}っているのに、つい{夜更|よふ}かしをしてしまう。
examples.english: Even though I intend to stop, I can't help staying up late.
examples.notes: つい〜てしまう pattern emphasizes lack of self-control

examples.english: They just came a moment ago.

examples.japanese: つい{先|さき}ほど{届|とど}きました。
examples.english: It arrived just a moment ago.

examples.japanese: ついこの{前|まえ}{会|あ}ったばかりなのに、もう{懐|なつ}かしい。
examples.english: We just met the other day, but I already feel nostalgic.

examples.japanese: つい{最近|さいきん}この{町|まち}に{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}してきたので、{近|ちか}くのお{店|みせ}をまだよく{知|し}らない。
examples.english: I just recently moved to this town, so I don't know the nearby shops well yet.

examples.japanese: つい{先日|せんじつ}{日本|にほん}に{来|き}たばかりだと{思|おも}っていたのに、もう3{年|ねん}も{経|た}っていて{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I thought I had just come to Japan, but I was surprised that three years had already passed.

notes:
つい expresses actions done without intending to, often with a nuance of regret or lack of self-control.

POSITION:
- Usually appears at the beginning of a clause, before the verb

COMMON PATTERNS:
- つい〜てしまう (end up doing ~ unintentionally)
- つい{先|さき}ほど (just a moment ago)
- つい{最近|さいきん} (just recently)

NUANCE:
- Implies the action was not fully intentional
- Often paired with てしまう to emphasize accidental nature
- Can express mild regret or excuse

SIMILAR WORDS:
- うっかり: carelessly, by mistake (more accidental)
- {思|おも}わず: involuntarily, without thinking (physical reflex)
